To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
48 states publicly report on at least one disability subgroup assessment, and 35 states publicly report on all of their state assessments.

(a) the majority of states publicly reported participation and performance data for their disability subgroups, (b) the number of states reporting participation and performance data increased between 2000— 2001 and 1 2001—2 2002, (c) the number of assessments for which participation and performance data were publicly reported increased between 2001—1 2002 and 2001 —2 2002 (although this increase was not statistically significant), (d)

1) the 48 states that publicly reported disability subgroup information in 2001-2002 reported participation information for 1.2 million students with disabilities and performance information for 1 million students with disabilities; 2) only 35 states publicly reported participation and performance information for all of their students with disabilities; and 3) 13 states did not report participation or performance information in 2002, and 2 states did not report any disability subgroup assessment data at all.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the extent to which states have met the requirements to publicly report on disability subgroup participation and performance on state assessments and the extent to which they have reported information for the full range of disability categories.
the extent to which states are publicly reporting on the performance of students with and without disabilities on statewide assessment.
the extent to which states have met the requirements to report participation and performance for students with disabilities.

the 48 states that reported disability subgroup assessment information in 2001—02 reported participation and performance information in ways that were consistent with IDEA requirements.
